title: Mechanisms of azole antifungal resistance in clinical isolates of Candida tropicalis.
authors: Paul, Saikat; Shaw, Dipika; Joshi, Himanshu; Singh, Shreya; Chakrabarti, Arunaloke; Rudramurthy, Shivaprakash M; Ghosh, Anup K
one_liner_zh: 该研究分析热带念珠菌唑类耐药机制，虽含ERG11同源建模与分子对接，但对象为真菌药物靶点蛋白-小分子配体互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或MD方法，与本课题TF-DNA结合研究无关。
abstract: This study was designed to understand the molecular mechanisms of azole resistance in Candida tropicalis using genetic and bioinformatics approaches. Thirty-two azole-resistant and 10 azole-susceptible (S) clinical isolates of C. tropicalis were subjected to mutation analysis of the azole target genes including ERG11. Inducible expression analysis of 17 other genes potentially associated with azole resistance was also evaluated. Homology modeling and molecular docking analysis were performed to study the effect of amino acid alterations in mediating azole resistance. Of the 32 resistant isolates, 12 (37.5%) showed A395T and C461T mutations in the ERG11 gene. The mean overexpression of CDR1, CDR3, TAC1, ERG1, ERG2, ERG3, ERG11, UPC2, and MKC1 in resistant isolates without mutation (R-WTM) was significantly higher (p<0.05) than those with mutation (R-WM) and the sensitive isolates (3.2-11 vs. 0.2-2.5 and 0.3-2.2 folds, respectively). Although the R-WTM and R-WM had higher (p<0.05) CDR2 and MRR1 expression compared to S isolates, noticeable variation was not seen among the other genes. Protein homology modelling and molecular docking revealed that the mutations in the ERG11 gene were responsible for structural alteration and low binding efficiency between ERG11p and ligands. Isolates with ERG11 mutations also presented A220C in ERG1 and together T503C, G751A mutations in UPC2. Nonsynonymous mutations in the ERG11 gene and coordinated overexpression of various genes including different transporters, ergosterol biosynthesis pathway, transcription factors, and stress-responsive genes are associated with azole resistance in clinical isolates of C. tropicalis.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在利用遗传学和生物信息学方法，探讨热带念珠菌（Candida tropicalis）对唑类耐药性的分子机制。对32株唑类耐药和10株唑类敏感（S）的临床分离热带念珠菌进行了唑类靶基因（包括ERG11）的突变分析，并评估了17个其他可能与唑类耐药相关基因的诱导表达分析。通过同源建模和分子对接分析，研究了氨基酸改变在介导唑类耐药中的作用。在32株耐药分离株中，12株（37.5%）在ERG11基因中表现出A395T和C461T突变。无突变耐药株（R-WTM）中CDR1、CDR3、TAC1、ERG1、ERG2、ERG3、ERG11、UPC2和MKC1的平均过表达水平显著高于（p<0.05）有突变耐药株（R-WM）和敏感株（分别为3.2-11倍 vs. 0.2-2.5倍和0.3-2.2倍）。尽管R-WTM和R-WM的CDR2和MRR1表达水平高于S株（p<0.05），但其他基因未见明显差异。蛋白质同源建模和分子对接显示，ERG11基因的突变导致ERG11p与配体之间的结构改变和结合效率降低。携带ERG11突变的分离株还表现出ERG1中的A220C突变，以及UPC2中的T503C、G751A突变。ERG11基因的非同义突变以及多种基因（包括不同转运蛋白、麦角固醇生物合成途径、转录因子和应激响应基因）的协调过表达，与热带念珠菌临床分离株的唑类耐药性相关。
